newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- US March PPI falls 0.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- US March PPI falls 0.1 percent.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. experts after the U.S. Labor Department said producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March compared to a 0.4 percent drop in February.

The core component, which excludes volatile food and energy components, rose 0.4 percent versus a 0.1 percent fall in the previous month. Experts in a Reuters survey had expected an unchanged reading for overall producer prices and a 0.1 percent rise in the core.

MELANIE HARDY, ECONOMIST, BEAR STEARNS & CO INC: "The PPI core rate was much higher than expected. But aircraft added 0.2 percent to the core rate and certainly aircraft doesn't appear in people's consumption basket so I don't think that is indicative of any sort of pickup in industrial prices.
"Away from the core number that was boosted by this one-time factor, it reconfirms that the industrial sector isn't overheating yet."
ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "(PPI) had a higher core than expected. Capital equipment was up, tobacco prices, car prices, it was a little of everything.
"There might be some more inflation in the pipeline than what we had thought. All in all, people are going to have to assume the (Federal Reserve) is going to have to tighten again."

MATT ALEXY, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON: "The PPI ex-food and energy at 0.4 pct is not very good so you have a series of rather significant events I'd argue as far as data are concerned.

"It's one of these things where the nuance of the numbers really comes and makes the day very difficult rather than just the headline whacking you over the head," Alexy noted of both the producer price and retail sales data.
